photos.caption: The Fram beset in the Arctic pack ice during the 1893-96 polar drift.
photos.credit: Fram Expedition / National Library of Norway

photos.caption: Fram in the pack ice, March 1894 — six months into the deliberate trans-arctic drift.
The supper table on board Fram during the long Arctic winter.
The Fram crew on the ice in a May 17th parade — Norway's constitution day, celebrated on the drifting floe.
photos.credit: Fram Expedition / National Library of Norway

photos.caption: Nansen and Johansen departing the Fram on 14 March 1895 to attempt the Pole on foot.
photos.credit: Fram Expedition / National Library of Norway

photos.caption: Nansen's farthest north — 86°13′6″ N — reached on 7 April 1895, the most northerly point yet attained by humans.
The first meeting with a stranger — Nansen's chance encounter with Frederick Jackson at Cape Flora, June 1896, after fifteen months alone with Johansen on Franz Josef Land.
photos.credit: Fram Expedition / National Library of Norway

photos.caption: Portrait of Fridtjof Nansen on his return from the Arctic, 1896.
